eu1.evidence: The EU AI Act classifies AI systems into **four risk tiers** — unacceptable, high, limited, and minimal risk.

eu2.evidence: High-risk systems must maintain detailed technical documentation and complete conformity assessments before EU deployment.

eu3.evidence: Real-time biometric identification in public spaces is prohibited except for **three narrow law enforcement exceptions**: (1) searching for missing children, (2) preventing specific and imminent terrorist threats, and (3) prosecuting serious crimes with post-judicial authorization.

eu4.evidence: Violations carry fines of up to **€35 million or 7% of global annual turnover**, whichever is higher.

eu5.evidence: AI-generated deepfakes must be clearly labeled as artificially generated, with technical standards defined by **ENISA**

cyber1.evidence: **zero-trust architecture** mandates continuous verification of every user and device.

cyber2.evidence: The **MITRE ATT&CK** framework catalogs **14 tactical categories** of adversary behavior.

cyber3.evidence: Supply chain attacks surged **742% between 2019–2022**, exemplified by the **SolarWinds Orion** compromise... affecting **18,000+ organizations** including US federal agencies.

cyber4.evidence: **NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0** added a sixth function — **Govern** — alongside Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, and Recover.

cyber5.evidence: Ransomware payments reached **$1.1 billion** globally in 2023, with average enterprise demands exceeding **$5.3 million** (Chainalysis).

mkt1.evidence: The global AI market is projected to reach **$1.8 trillion by 2030** at a **~37% CAGR**.

mkt2.evidence: Multi-agent AI adoption is concentrated in **financial services (34%)**, healthcare, and manufacturing.

mkt3.evidence: Deploying AI agents delivers a **median 23% operational cost reduction** but requires a **40% infrastructure spending increase** during the first 18 months

mkt4.evidence: McKinsey estimates generative AI could add **$2.6–$4.4 trillion annually** across **63 enterprise use cases**, with banking and retail capturing the largest share.

mkt5.evidence: Only **11% of enterprises** have moved beyond pilot stage. Barriers: **67% cite integration complexity**, **54% cite governance concerns**.

ir1.evidence: The **NIST Incident Response Lifecycle** defines four phases: Preparation; Detection and Analysis; Containment, Eradication, and Recovery; and Post-Incident Activity.

ir2.evidence: In 2023, mean time to identify a breach was **204 days** plus **73 days** to contain (IBM).

ir3.evidence: Organizations with IR teams and tested plans saved **$2.66 million per breach**.

ir4.evidence: Average breach cost: **$4.45 million** globally; **$10.93 million** in healthcare — the highest of any industry.

ir5.evidence: AI/automation reduced costs by **$1.76 million** and shortened the breach lifecycle by **108 days**.

gov1.evidence: The **OECD AI Principles** (adopted by **46+ countries**) establish five core values: inclusive growth, human-centered values, transparency, robustness, and accountability.

gov2.evidence: **ISO/IEC 42001** is the first international standard for AI management systems.

gov3.evidence: The **Singapore Model AI Governance Framework** recommends tiered testing with **human-in-the-loop** escalation for high-impact decisions.

ops1.evidence: **Gartner** predicts **33% of enterprise software** will include agentic AI by **2028**, up from **<1% in 2024**.

ops2.evidence: **Infosys** reports AI-driven automation achieves **35–45% faster procurement cycle times**, with peak gains in vendor onboarding and invoice reconciliation.
